title: Initiate the Continuity One shared-setting shell
scope: Establishes only the stable setting identity, proposed shell, shared-core authority topology, and unanswered layered constitutional decision map for setting://continuity-one; establishes no fictional world, work, character, protagonist, plot, outline, chapter, or manuscript facts.
approval_evidence: The Author explicitly selected SET-INIT1A, SET-INIT2A, and SET-INIT3A on 2026-08-12.
question: What stable identity, cross-work authority topology, and constitutional scope should initiate the first real shared setting without establishing fictional canon?
selection: SET-INIT1A, SET-INIT2A, and SET-INIT3A: stable setting://continuity-one identity with provisional display title; one shared core with governed compatible work-local overlays; and a layered but unanswered foundation decision map.
alternatives: SET-INIT1B: choose a fiction-bearing title now and derive the permanent slug.
SET-INIT1C: postpone initialization pending a non-canonical naming brief.
SET-INIT2B: require every setting fact to live only in shared canon.
SET-INIT2C: begin with explicitly branching continuities.
SET-INIT3B: use only a minimal authority charter.
SET-INIT3C: predefine exhaustive approval surfaces for every anticipated domain.
rationale: A neutral stable identity permits setting-first development without prematurely encoding fictional assumptions. A shared core supports consistency across later works while scoped overlays preserve local flexibility. An unanswered layered map exposes dependencies without silently deciding them.
evidence: Author selections SET-INIT1A, SET-INIT2A, and SET-INIT3A on 2026-08-12.
consequences: Create the isolated worldbuilding/settings/continuity-one setting shell as DRAFT/PROPOSED.
Keep adopting_work_ids empty until a separately approved work adopts the setting.
Permit future work-local overlays to add compatible facts; require a separate Author decision for any proposed contradiction or override.
Leave all fictional foundation layers unanswered for later SETTING_AUTHORITY decisions.
Leave WLD-SOUL-001A and WLD-PRENATAL-001A unadopted and unassumed.
residual_unknowns: Every fictional question in the layered foundation decision map.
Whether any future work adopts a project-level default.
Which future work, if any, first adopts the setting.
reopening_conditions: The Author chooses a different stable setting identity or authority topology.
A later approved continuity model requires branching shared authorities.
Repository governance changes the setting-first authoring boundary.
